title: Write the checks that catch a lost hold

blocks.text: A prepaid card can't spend more than its balance. `HoldFunds` takes the purchase amount off the card while the issuer decides, and must give it back when the purchase doesn't go through. An earlier version passed every test the team had, and still lost cardholders' money in production.

The team's checks are in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/HoldFundsChecks.java`. The tests run them against a real TransactionManager whose chain is `HoldFunds`, an issuer stand-in and `SendResponse`, each check on a fresh chain (the `Chain` interface says what a check can do). `approvedPurchase` is written. Finish the two checks marked `TODO`, so that a correct `HoldFunds` passes all three, and a `HoldFunds` that gets the cardholder's money or the terminal's answer wrong fails at least one. The tests try several wrong versions. About ten lines in total.

cases.says: the checks pass for a HoldFunds that answers every purchase and leaves each card with the right balance
the checks fail for a HoldFunds that votes NO_JOIN after holding the money, so the real TransactionManager never gives it back when the issuer declines
the checks fail for a HoldFunds whose own refusal joins and whose abort credits an amount it never held
the checks fail for a HoldFunds that refuses without leaving a response, because the terminal then gets nothing

origin.section: 11.2 Only the Real TransactionManager Decides Who Hears the Outcome

concepts: A test that calls commit or abort by hand checks its author's idea of the TransactionManager; the vote decides who hears the outcome, so the whole vote is asserted and the abort path is tested through the real TransactionManager.
